top_strength: This is the best discovery work in the batch. She ran a genuinely complete intake: both zip codes, square footage, bedroom count, one-story to two-story, driveway versus street at both ends, the incline, packing responsibility, a box estimate she anchored for the customer ("usually for residence your size on average, I think we see around like 40, 45"), specialty items, additional stops, and then a full walk of the non-boxed inventory that surfaced the crib, two dressers, couch and love seat, two desks, twelve cube shelves, TV stand, queen bed, and the purple mattress. She closed discovery with the textbook stressors question — "do you have any specific concerns or stressors about the moving process in general that I can address for you?" — which almost nobody asks. She also built real rapport off the pinball machine, telling the customer she had moved both a pinball table and an arcade cabinet herself, which got a "Cool" back.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: quote this move on the phone. She did all the hard work — she had square footage, bedroom count, stairs, access, box count, and a full inventory — and then handed the entire pricing conversation to an email, so the customer hung up not knowing our hourly rate, our minimum, or a single differentiator. At 1,100 sq ft this move does not require a walkthrough, so the transition should have been "Great, I've got everything I need — let me walk you through pricing right now, it's super simple," then rate, what's included, the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute proration, No Worries at $2,000, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee, and only then "I'll put all of that in an email so you have it in writing." Second priority: no booking attempt at all. She confirmed the date was open and let it sit — "we do have availability on the 9th, and Fridays in October fill up fast; there's no deposit, so I can hold that for you right now" costs nothing and is the whole point of the call. Third: run Save Your Ass here — 40–50 boxes, a shed, and twelve cube shelves is exactly the move where prep time converts into a lower bill. Two live business risks: she verbally confirmed availability for "August 9th" when the customer asked for October 9th, so if she checked the calendar against a past date the availability confirmation is meaningless and the estimate email may carry the wrong move date — this needs to be verified in EMMA before that email goes out. And she let the customer plan to pre-disassemble the pinball machine herself without telling her disassembly and reassembly are included, so the customer is doing unnecessary work and we lost a differentiator moment.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and natural — used Morgan's name three times, reacted to what the customer actually said, and built real rapport swapping pinball-moving stories, though heavy "gotcha" filler and one dropped-thread moment kept it short of outstanding.
